messages:
jesse: Heads-up — after the kernel rollout to 6.1.12 on ap-southeast1 ampere pools we're seeing large P2P performance variance. Spike in tail latency for multi-GPU inference jobs and some nodes report P2P OFF. Starting thread to collect quick telemetry.

sasha: Oof. Which node ids/labels? Any pattern (AZ, rack)?

jesse: Mostly ampere-asea-{02,03,07,11}. Not all hosts in the same AZ. Throughput drops ~30-50% on multi-GPU batches. Single-GPU seems fine.

jamal: Pasted nvidia topo and dmesg from ampere-asea-03:
```
$ nvidia-smi topo -m
        GPU0    GPU1    CPU Affinity
GPU0     X      NV1     0-31
GPU1    NV1      X      0-31

NV1 = Not Supported (P2P disabled)
```
and kernel dmesg: 
```
[   12.345678] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: PCIe ACS capability enabled, redirected upstream
[   12.345679] nvidia-mig: p2p_disabled=1
```

priya: lspci -vvv grepped ACS on same host:
```
01:00.0 VGA compatible controller: NVIDIA Corporation Device XXXX (rev a1)
	Capabilities: [100 v1] Express (v3) Endpoint, MSI 00
	LnkCtl: ASPM Disabled; RCB 64 bytes
	Vendor Specific: ACS: Redirected
```

lena: That ACS "Redirected" bit being set sounds like the kernel vendor backported stricter ACS enforcement that prevents P2P for those PCIe functions. We saw something similar in an older driver/kernel combo months ago. Quick mitigation options: 1) drain and revert kernel on affected nodes, 2) move heavy multi-GPU work to dedicated fallback pool, 3) enable a compatibility shim if present in driver.

jesse: We need a triage path that doesn't overload other regions. ap-southeast has limited spare capacity. Suggest immediate: cordon + schedule small canary rollback for 2 nodes, then if OK roll back remaining.

deploy-bot: New rollout ticket created: RB-2741 — ap-southeast1 Ampere kernel rollback canary (2 nodes). Link: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/RB-2741

ops-bot: Alert: Capacity alert triggered for ap-southeast1: 85% GPU utilization; fallback-pool available with 12 GPUs at 1.8x cost.

priya: Also, check kernel module option for NVIDIA to override P2P? Not ideal but worth verifying. On affected host tried: 
```
sudo modprobe nvidia NVreg_EnablePeerAccess=1
# reboot required for some flags
```
Result: no change — ACS is handled at PCI layer so driver can't re-enable hardware-level P2P once ACS redirects.

jamal: Confirmed via run of nv_peer_mem tests — cross-GPU memcpy falls back to staging copy path and performance tanked. Profiling: 420us -> 1.2ms per large chunk.

lena: Commands I'm going to run for the canary rollback:
```
kubectl cordon ampere-asea-02
kubectl drain ampere-asea-02 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data\# trigger rollback job
./infra/tools/rollout-kernel --hosts ampere-asea-02 --version 5.15.89 --reason "P2P regression"
```

sasha: If we drain, also ensure GPU reservations for realtime customers are honored. I'll update cost-mitigation channel for temporary capacity shift.

jesse: Long-term: vendor ticket to get rationale for ACS bit set on these endpoints. Could be PCIe switch firmware path where the kernel enables ACS on some downstream ports. Opened internal bug RB-2742 for vendor escalation and logs attached.

priya: One odd datapoint — some hosts with identical PCIe switch model didn't get the ACS redirect set. Suspect subtle BIOS/firmware differences or hotpatch ordering during upgrade.

jamal: For visibility I've added a Grafana panel to track NV P2P status by host (topo/matrix -> string match 'Not Supported'). Link: https://grafana.redwood/board/p2p-hosts

lena: Can we do a quick smoke on the rollback node once it's back? I'll run a scripted multi-GPU tiny-batch job: 
```
python perf/run_infer.py --model llama-7b --batch 8 --gpus 2 --iters 50 --collect-latency
```

deploy-bot: RB-2741 canary rollback scheduled in 10m window.

sasha: Action plan summary:
- [x] create rollback ticket RB-2741
- [x] add Grafana panel for P2P hosts
- [ ] run canary rollback on ampere-asea-02 (lena)
- [ ] validate perf (jamal/lena)
- [ ] if green, roll remaining affected nodes (jesse)
- [ ] vendor escalation RB-2742 (priya)

jesse: Thx team. I'll coordinate capacity shifts and cost alerts. If rollback goes bad we may need to route load to higher-cost fallback pool — please flag immediate SLA risk if that happens. :pray:

lena: Canary rollback completed & node back. Preliminary perf looks restored on ampere-asea-02. Leaving cordon until we validate more nodes.

jamal: Verified: multi-GPU latency is back to baseline on the canary host. nv_peer_mem shows direct P2P link available.

sasha: Ok, proceed with staged rollbacks but throttle to 2 hosts per hour to avoid capacity shock. I'll post schedule.

priya: Filing follow-up: check firmware inventory across ampere nodes and ensure kernel packaging includes release notes about ACS behavior.

jesse: Closing loop later today with a postmortem draft (will link here). Great quick work.
